messages:
jamie: Heads-up — planned maintenance tonight 02:00–04:00 UTC for phoenix-gpu-pool (rack phx-07). We'll perform staggered node drains to flash NIC firmware and do graceful reboots. Expect a temporary ~20% drop in burstable capacity while we hand off jobs. Full plan + rollback below. @ops-oncall please ack.

ev an: acked. are we doing a canary first or do we rotate evenly across the rack?

jamie: Canary first — gpu-node-137 will be the canary. If stable for 15m, continue 1 node at a time. Rotation order pinned in runbook: phx-07 -> phx-08 -> phx-09 etc.

sofia: Adding KV-cache pre-seed on the target pool before bringing nodes back to avoid cold-cache latency spikes. I recommend seeding the two hottest prefixes.

kim: Any customer-facing impact? Dedicated tenants pinned to other pools should be unaffected, right?

jamie: Correct — Dedicated pinned pools unaffected. Hosted burst traffic may see longer queue wait if we hit the 20% capacity dip. We'll enable temporary routing to burst-reserve pool (phoenix-burst1) for short bursts; note cost tradeoff below.

ops-oncall: I'm on overnight duty and will be present on the channel. Will monitor alerts and escalate if node reboots take >10m.

deploy-bot: Maintenance window created: 2026-03-23T02:00:00Z -> 2026-03-23T04:00:00Z (ID: mw-1798888888). Auto-notify enabled for affected teams. :calendar:

jamie: Quick checklist (copy to runbook):
```
# canary node flow
kubectl cordon gpu-node-137
kubectl drain gpu-node-137 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=120
flash-nic-fw --node gpu-node-137 --fw-version v2.1.4 --verify-checksum
reboot-node gpu-node-137 --wait 300
run-health-checks --node gpu-node-137 --checks net/rx, pcie, kernel-logs
kubectl uncordon gpu-node-137
# if health checks fail: rollback firmware and uncordon, mark node for manual debug
```

sofia: KV seed commands (after uncordon):
```
phoenix-cache-seed --pool phoenix-gpu-pool --prefix \"/models/large\" --workers 4
phoenix-cache-seed --pool phoenix-gpu-pool --prefix \"/chat/active_sessions\" --workers 2
```

evan: Cost note: if we need to route to phoenix-burst1 for the duration, estimate extra infra spend ~~$3.8k for the 2h window (preemptible + bandwidth). Recommend approval from finance for contingency.

kim: Can we compress the window to 90m if canary looks solid? Ops-oncall, any objection to a dynamic rollback-that-extends plan?

ops-oncall: No objection. We'll hold 30m after canary before accelerating. If anything abnormal, we stop and rollback.

jamie: Communication plan: post banner to status.redwood.com 30m before start, 15m reminder in #customer-success, and an email to top-10 tenants with potential burst impact. Put a note in console route: \"phoenix-gpu-pool — maintenance\".

sofia: I'll add a quick eval run after canary to check output quality vs baseline.

evan: One more ask — please annotate the nodes in k8s with fw-version after successful run so we can query fleet state easily.

jamie: Will do: `kubectl annotate node gpu-node-137 redwood/fw=v2.1.4`

kim: ack (finance pinged for contingency). :thumbsup:

ops-oncall: I'll publish a short postmortem template in the thread if anything goes off-nominal.

jamie: Thanks everyone. I'll paste the final runbook link here when I finish edits: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/phoenix-pool-maint-1798888888

deploy-bot: Reminder scheduled: 30m pre-notify at 2026-03-23T01:30:00Z.

sofia: thanks — leaving a quick note: watch p99 latency and token-per-second during the first 10 min after each node returns.

jamie: end of plan. :white_check_mark:
